cultural_entities.translation_note: The translation renders this as 'The Division of the Monkey', which captures the literal meaning but loses the immediate cultural association with the Panchatantra/Jataka fable of the monkey who arbitrates a dispute between two cats only to eat all the bread himself.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The title 'Bandar Bant' refers to a well-known folk tale of a monkey dividing bread between two cats and eating it all himself. The English translation 'The Division of the Monkey' loses this cultural allusion to deceptive mediation and division.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The phrase 'lakeer kheenchna' (drawing a line) is a common idiom in South Asian languages representing the drawing of an uncrossable boundary or limit. The translation 'drew a line' is literal but loses the idiomatic weight of establishing an absolute, unyielding boundary.

original_poem:
बंदर बंट

हम सब मिलकर एक जंगल में रहते थे।
वो भी हमारी तरह ही बनते थे।
कभी एक, कभी दो, कभी तीन होते थे,
बेशक हम जंगल के सबसे बड़े लीडर थे।
 
लेकिन किसी दिन हमने देखा जंगल के पास में,
बहुत से अन्य छोटे चूहे आ गए थे,
जो सबने मिलकर हमारे लिए खींची एक लकीर,
और उस लकीर के उस पार हम नहीं जाते थे।
translated_poem:
The Division of the Monkey

We all lived together in the forest.  
They, too, were like us.  
Sometimes one, sometimes two, sometimes three,  
We were undoubtedly the greatest leaders of the forest.  

But one day we saw near the jungle,  
A lot of smaller mice came,  
Who together drew a line for us,  
And beyond that line, we were not allowed to go.
